journey.title: Focus stays in the basket dialog after removing a row
journey.goal: Removing the row that holds the focused button keeps keyboard focus inside the trapped dialog

plan.root_cause: When a focused element inside the focus trap is removed from the DOM, the trap's cached tabbable-node list becomes stale. The mutation‑observer callback that detects the removal calls getInitialFocusNode() using the stale cache, which may return a detached node. Trying to focus a detached node is a no‑op, so focus remains outside the trap (e.g., on the body).
plan.repair_strategy: In the mutation‑observer's checkDomRemoval handler, call updateTabbableNodes() before attempting to restore focus. This ensures the cached tabbable nodes reflect the current DOM state, allowing getInitialFocusNode() to return a valid node inside the trap.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard focus will remain trapped inside the basket dialog after removing an item, ensuring that sequential tab navigation stays within the dialog and does not escape to the page background.
functional_risks: Calling updateTabbableNodes on each removal adds a small performance overhead.
If updateTabbableNodes inadvertently triggers further DOM mutations, it could cause redundant observer callbacks, but the trap guards against re‑entrancy.
The change assumes updateTabbableNodes is safe to call while the trap is active; misuse could lead to incorrect state if called at inappropriate times.
verification_requirements: After focusing a remove button inside the basket and pressing Enter to delete its row, focus must stay inside the basket (e.g., on the close button or another item's remove button).
Opening the basket, tabbing through its controls, and closing it must continue to work as before.
The item count must update correctly after each removal.
No regression in other pages that use the focus‑trap component.

plan.root_cause: The mutation observer's checkDomRemoval handler only detects direct removal of the focused node. When a list item containing the focused button is removed, the button is not in removedNodes (only its ancestor li is), so the trap fails to restore focus and focus escapes to the body.
plan.repair_strategy: Update checkDomRemoval to also check if any removed node contains the focused node (using Node.contains). Also refresh the tabbable node cache by calling updateTabbableNodes before attempting to restore focus.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard focus remains trapped inside the basket dialog after a row removal, allowing continued tab navigation within the dialog and preventing focus from escaping to the page background.
functional_risks: The containment check adds a minor performance cost per mutation.
If the focused node is in a detached subtree, Node.contains might behave unexpectedly, but the node is in the same document.
verification_requirements: After focusing a remove button inside the basket and pressing Enter to delete its row, focus must stay inside the basket (e.g., on the close button or another item's remove button).
Opening the basket, tabbing through its controls, and closing it must continue to work as before.
The item count must update correctly after each removal.
No regression in other pages that use the focus-trap component.
